comparability.note: the original 4096 k*G and 4096 k*P population, at seed 0x5046503250485032, reproduces the digests recorded at the same two DSOs in dso-differential-pfp20/raw, so the added classes did not change the comparable population

identity_proof.method: each process printed LOADED realpath/dev/ino/size for the file it mapped and LIB from dladdr(BN_new); the runner compared those fields with stat(2) on the expected on-disk DSO and required a /proc/self/maps entry

instrument.instrument_note: The loader, identity proof and serialised-point comparison are the PFP-2 court instrument (pfp2_dso_differential.c, sha256 fd67b943889ab710af9f3c246e3119c2f28561dc6a47084ee96f5a5d5f64affc). Only the population generator was extended; the original mul-g/mul-p modes reproduce the original bytes and line format.
instrument.loader_pattern: dlopen(RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL), one libcrypto.so.3 per process; LOADED/MAPS/LIB checked against stat(2), unchanged from pfp2_dso_differential.c
instrument.serialisation: EC_POINT_point2oct(POINT_CONVERSION_UNCOMPRESSED); the original modes require 65 bytes, the population classes record the actual SEC1 length so the point at infinity (one 0x00 byte) is compared rather than treated as a failure

limitations: Internal field operations (p256::mont_reduce_into, p256::wide_mul_x86, limbs::normalise_branchless) have no exported entry point and were not called directly; they are exercised only through EC_POINT_mul and EC_POINT_oct2point. No source-level test is substituted while this court is called DSO-bound.
P-256 has prime group order n, so it has no non-trivial small-order point; the only order-1 point is infinity, exercised as an input base and as a result.

2q-1 does not fit in 32 bytes and is supplied to EC_POINT_mul as a 33-byte BIGNUM; the API accepts arbitrary-precision scalars and does not reject out-of-range values, so agreement is on the computed result, and the only rejection compared is an off-curve point decode.
The candidate is the frozen distribution DSO; it was not rebuilt in this court. Its digest is checked before and after execution.
This is a compatibility/correctness court. It is not a constant-time result and not a safety conclusion.
